sections.title: Paul in Corinth
observations: Paul arrives in Corinth, a major city known for its commerce and immorality. Here, he meets Aquila and Priscilla, fellow tentmakers who become his companions in ministry.
The significance of Paul working as a tentmaker highlights the importance of self-sufficiency in ministry, as well as the value of building relationships with fellow believers.
Paul's preaching in the synagogue leads to both acceptance and opposition, illustrating the mixed responses to the Gospel.

sections.title: Opposition and Encouragement
observations: Paul faces opposition from the Jews in Corinth, leading him to focus on the Gentiles. This shift emphasizes the expanding mission of the church beyond the Jewish community.
God reassures Paul in a vision, encouraging him to continue speaking boldly. This divine encouragement is crucial for sustaining ministry in the face of adversity.

sections.title: Paul's Return to Antioch
observations: After a year and a half in Corinth, Paul departs for Syria, taking Priscilla and Aquila with him. This journey signifies the ongoing mission of the church and the importance of sending out workers.
In Ephesus, Paul briefly preaches in the synagogue before continuing his journey, demonstrating the urgency of spreading the Gospel.

sections.title: Apollos in Ephesus
observations: Apollos, an eloquent speaker and knowledgeable in the Scriptures, arrives in Ephesus. His initial understanding of the Gospel is incomplete, as he only knows the baptism of John.
Priscilla and Aquila take Apollos aside to explain the way of God more accurately, highlighting the importance of sound teaching and mentorship in the church.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord speaks to Paul in a vision, encouraging him to continue his work in Corinth without fear, emphasizing God's presence and support in ministry.
Priscilla and Aquila's instruction of Apollos demonstrates the importance of teaching and correcting in the church, ensuring that the message of the Gospel is accurately conveyed.

questions: What does Paul's experience in Corinth teach us about facing opposition in ministry?
How can we apply the principle of mentorship seen in Priscilla and Aquila's relationship with Apollos to our own lives?
What does God's encouragement to Paul reveal about His character and involvement in our lives during difficult times?
